small_guidance:
- The current gather-based ConvTranspose loops over (KH, KW) with valid masks that drop ~75% of work at stride=2; restructure the spatial decomposition by fixing the (oh%stride, ow%stride) parity per program so each (kh,kw) maps to a single valid (ih,iw) without masking, eliminating wasted FLOPs.
- Try larger GEMM tiles biased toward the OH_OW dimension (BLOCK_SP=128/256, BLOCK_OC=64, BLOCK_IC=64) with num_warps=8, num_stages=3 — output spatial is 256×256=65536, so SP tiling dominates locality; also add a BLOCK_OC=32/BLOCK_SP=256 config.
- Hoist the per-(kh,kw) W-load out of the IC loop by accumulating into one acc per (kh,kw) only when valid — or better, swap loop order so IC is the outer accumulator and (kh,kw) inner, allowing a single x-tile load reused across kh,kw of W.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as a scatter-add kernel: one program per (N, IC tile, IH*IW tile) computing the input×kernel outer product and atomically scattering into the output grid. This avoids the divisibility mask waste of the gather formulation (3/4 of iterations currently produce zero contribution at stride=2).
- Alternatively, use a gather kernel that's parameterized per output-pixel parity: launch (stride*stride) separate logical sub-grids where each sub-grid handles outputs with a fixed (oh%stride, ow%stride); for each parity only ceil(KH/stride)*ceil(KW/stride) kernel taps contribute, all unconditionally valid, turning the inner loop into a dense small GEMM with no validity mask.
- Use channels_last (NHWC) layout for both x and out so the IC axis becomes the contiguous GEMM-K dim; preload W into shared/registers once per program since W is tiny (64×64×3×3 = 36KB) and reused across all spatial tiles.
